key_insight: Quantum generative models can learn a Langevin potential instead of circuit rotations, using Fokker–Planck solvers to prepare states that encode probability distributions.
engineering_relevance: This physics-informed design offers a route to trainable quantum models for scientific distributions, with explicit circuit constructions and resource analysis.
method: Parameterize the Langevin potential and Hermitianize its Fokker–Planck equation.
Solve using a linear combination of cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation.
Encode the square root of the stationary density and sample through computational-basis measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter recovery for multivariate distributions and dimension-independent, sample-efficient convex optimization for in-distribution targets, but provides no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: The training guarantees apply to in-distribution targets; practical scalability also depends on block-encoding and quantum solver resource costs.
paper_title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
